html:
SMTO-ART-0002 — SMTO couldn't add or list files in the task's Artifacts

GUID: d16c7a5c-1e6c-468d-87da-f58a72c78e74
Slug: artifact-registration-failed
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • During the task, SMTO tried to add a file to the task's Artifacts, or to list them, and that step failed. The file itself may still be where the task created it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the task to finish, then open its Artifacts list and check whether the file is already there. SMTO also collects files automatically, so the file may have been saved even though this step failed.
  2. If the Artifacts list shows Retry collection, select it. That tries again to save the files this task created, without running the task's commands again.
  3. If the file is still missing, ask SMTO in the same conversation to save it to Artifacts again, naming the file. Naming the file makes sure the right one is saved, and you've already confirmed it isn't there.
  4. If the message says artifact storage is unavailable, make sure the computer running SMTO has free disk space before asking again. SMTO stores each saved file in its data folder and can't add new ones when it can't write there.

What success looks like

  • The file appears once in the task's Artifacts list and can be downloaded.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep asking SMTO to save the same file over and over before the cause is fixed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The artifact capability (artifact.register, list or get) caught an ArtifactError, ValueError or OSError before changing any artifact metadata and returned artifact_registration_failed; an OSError is reported as 'Artifact storage is unavailable.'

What this means

  • The artifact capability catches ArtifactError or OSError while registering an output or listing the run's artifacts and returns its safe failure wrapper. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • The artifact capability catches ArtifactError or OSError while registering an output or listing the run's artifacts and returns its safe failure wrapper.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the underlying artifact kind and selected operation; the wrapper does not identify one specific disk or integrity cause.

How to fix it

  • Read the step's error and its ArtifactError error_kind (for example artifact_run_required, artifact_active_writers, or a path outside the run's output workspace), or the Server log for the OSError. Fix storage space or permissions under the Server artifact store, or the path, list the run's artifacts to confirm the file is not already registered, then register it again.
  • Inspect the specific artifact/OS diagnostic and reconcile any existing registration before collecting again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended artifact operation succeeds through its supported owning registry.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
